rows.does: Splits the picture into thread colours and sews each colour area as fill or satin, with joins, underlay and pull from the fabric.
rows.use: Flat-colour logos, badges, cartoons, illustrations, anything that must keep its background or several colours.
rows.avoid: Real photos and portraits (use photo_lines); thin line drawings (fills lose lines under 1 mm).
rows.limits: 2 to 8 colours. Parts thinner than about 1 mm vanish unless line_details brings them back.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Sews light lines on a dark background as running stitches; the dark background stays bare fabric.
rows.use: Chalk, neon or white line drawings on black, line icons.
rows.avoid: Art with filled areas or a background that must be stitched.
rows.limits: One thread. line_retrace_mm sets how far it may travel back over sewn lines to save cuts.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Sews the black lines of a drawing; white stays bare fabric.
rows.use: Clean black ink line drawings on a plain white background.
rows.avoid: Shaded art, pencil, engravings, halftone or textured backgrounds: shading turns into specks and a honeycomb of lines (use photo_lines).
rows.limits: One thread. Filled black areas become heavy dense lines.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Sews rows of zigzag whose width follows the shading, as one continuous thread with few cuts.
rows.use: Real photos, portraits, pets, shaded black-and-white art.
rows.avoid: Flat logos and text, which look blurry in rows.
rows.limits: One thread colour. row_mm 0.6 to 2 (smaller = more detail and stitches). light_thread for light thread on dark fabric.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Rows of fill stitches with staggered needle holes and underlay; the standard fill.
rows.use: Any area wider than about 8 mm, backgrounds, large shapes. The safe default.
rows.avoid: Thin parts under about 1.5 mm wide (use satin or a line).
rows.limits: Row direction can be set per area; rows across the long side of an area pull it less.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Tatami with needle holes stepped in a chevron, so the rows show a faint zigzag texture.
rows.use: Large fills that look too flat, backgrounds with a subtle texture.
rows.avoid: Small areas, where the texture cannot show.
rows.limits: Same density and pull as tatami.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Rows go from full density on one side to open spacing (1.6 mm) on the other, so the fabric shows through.
rows.use: Fades, skies, light effects, lighter stitch count on big areas.
rows.avoid: Areas that must look solid; dark fabric under a light thread where the open side looks dirty.
rows.limits: No underlay. Sections are cut, never travelled across, so it can add cuts.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: The area's tatami plus a gradient in a 30% darker shade across it, for depth.
rows.use: Round or soft shapes that need shading in a flat-colour design (petals, leaves, balls).
rows.avoid: Designs that must keep few colours: it adds one more thread.
rows.limits: One extra colour change per shaded area colour.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Rays from the centre of the area outward.
rows.use: Round shapes: suns, flower centres, buttons, eyes.
rows.avoid: Long or irregular shapes; it falls back to tatami when rays cover under 85% of the area.
rows.limits: Dense at the centre; best on areas roughly as wide as they are tall.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Rows that rise and fall in smooth waves.
rows.use: Water, flags, hair, decorative backgrounds.
rows.avoid: Small areas where the wave cannot show.
rows.limits: Same density as tatami.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Rows follow the curve of the area's top edge.
rows.use: Curved bands, arches, petals and leaves where rows should follow the shape.
rows.avoid: Shapes with a ragged or very steep top edge.
rows.limits: Steep ends of the curve are flattened.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: A fabric piece instead of stitches: placement line, machine stop to lay the fabric, tack-down, stop to trim, then a satin edge (3 mm by default). Needler also writes a cutting file.
rows.use: Big solid areas on patches, jackets, blankets, kids' designs; saves many stitches.
rows.avoid: Small or thin parts (hard to cut and lay); caps and stretchy fabric.
rows.limits: 2 machine stops per piece. The person must cut and place fabric during sewing.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: partial: the fabric runs about 1.5 mm on under the parts sewn on top of it, and that edge gets no satin. combine: pieces of one colour are placed, tacked down and covered together, so 2 stops in all instead of 2 per piece. join: where two appliqué pieces meet, only the later piece's satin covers the join.
rows.use: partial when an appliqué piece lies under stitched details (a face on a fabric head); combine when there are several pieces of one fabric; join when pieces touch, to avoid a double satin edge.
rows.avoid: partial when the part on top is thin (the fabric only runs under parts wide enough to hide it); combine when the person wants to lay each piece separately.
rows.limits: Colour mode only. Works on parts styled applique; each piece stays at least 6 mm across.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Long smooth stitches across the shape that follow its direction; shiny and raised.
rows.use: Narrow parts: lettering strokes, borders, stems, outlines, small shapes 1.5 to 8 mm wide.
rows.avoid: Areas wider than 8 mm (loose, snag); very thin parts under about 1 mm.
rows.limits: Parts up to 8 mm wide. Stitches longer than 7 mm are auto-split with staggered holes. Underlay chosen by width.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Three satin layers stacked for a raised look, without foam.
rows.use: Small raised accents, initials, on firm fabric.
rows.avoid: Wide, curved or branching shapes; stretchy fabric.
rows.limits: Experimental. Needs a straight band shape.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Satin over foam; the machine stops so the foam can be placed, the satin cuts through it and the foam stays raised.
rows.use: When the person asks for puff, foam, raised or 3D: bold lettering and outlines, especially on caps.
rows.avoid: Big solid areas, fine detail, thin parts.
rows.limits: Parts 3 to 6 mm wide on 3 mm foam (2 to 6 mm on 2 mm foam); wider or thinner parts stay flat. One stop per puff colour.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Small repeated shapes sewn as running stitch across the area; open fill.
rows.use: Light decorative fills, quilt-like textures, backgrounds where the fabric may show.
rows.avoid: Areas that must look solid; small areas (too small for the pattern).
rows.limits: Choices: diamonds, hearts, stars, scales, circles. At most 400 pattern cells per area.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Repeated shapes that stretch to follow the area's top and bottom edges; open fill.
rows.use: Decorative bands and curved shapes where the pattern should bend with the shape.
rows.avoid: Solid-looking areas; small or round areas.
rows.limits: Same choices as Motif.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Tatami with a diamond overlay that presses a texture into it.
rows.use: Textured solid areas: leather looks, quilted backgrounds.
rows.avoid: Small areas; designs that need few stitches.
rows.limits: Experimental texture; more stitches than tatami.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Tatami with needle holes placed in a diamond lattice, so a quilted pattern shows in the fill.
rows.use: Large solid fills that should carry a subtle pattern.
rows.avoid: Small areas, where the lattice cannot show.
rows.limits: Same density as tatami.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Tatami rows whose ends are uneven, like fur or feathers.
rows.use: Animal fur, feathers, grass, soft edges that blend into the next colour.
rows.avoid: Logos with crisp edges.
rows.limits: Choices: one edge, both edges, textured edge.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Tatami whose rows tighten towards the edges, so the area looks domed.
rows.use: Balls, planets, eyes, round shapes that should look curved.
rows.avoid: Flat logos.
rows.limits: Areas under 4 mm across fall back to tatami.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Uneven stitches in open rows, like hand sewing; open fill.
rows.use: Hand-made, rustic or folk looks.
rows.avoid: Areas that must cover the fabric.
rows.limits: Open fill: the fabric shows.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Concentric rings spiralling from the centre outward.
rows.use: Round shapes, water drops, targets, decorative circles.
rows.avoid: Long thin areas.
rows.limits: Best on round, compact areas.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: One line winding like a labyrinth through the area; open fill.
rows.use: Light decorative texture, quilt looks.
rows.avoid: Areas that must look solid.
rows.limits: Open fill: the fabric shows.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: A star-shaped spiral from the centre; open fill.
rows.use: Decorative round areas, festive designs.
rows.avoid: Areas that must look solid; long areas.
rows.limits: Open fill: the fabric shows.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Rows follow the area's outline inward, ring by ring, around holes.
rows.use: Shapes where rows should echo the outline: letters with holes, frames, organic shapes.
rows.avoid: Very large areas (many rings, many stitches).
rows.limits: Same density as tatami.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Diagonal crosses on a grid clipped to the area; open fill.
rows.use: Cross-stitch looks, folk and pixel art.
rows.avoid: Small or thin areas; solid coverage.
rows.limits: Open fill: the fabric shows.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: One meandering line through the area; open fill.
rows.use: Quilting looks, light backgrounds, texture behind other parts.
rows.avoid: Areas that must look solid.
rows.limits: Choices: single run, backstitch, stemstitch (heavier lines).
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: A lattice of straight lines every 4 mm with diagonals; open fill.
rows.use: Traditional blackwork looks, light geometric backgrounds.
rows.avoid: Areas that must look solid.
rows.limits: Open fill: the fabric shows.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Raised knots in rows, 4 mm apart; open fill.
rows.use: Vintage, quilt and cushion looks.
rows.avoid: Small areas; solid coverage.
rows.limits: Many stitches per knot.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: A honeycomb net with 2 mm sides; open fill.
rows.use: Lace looks, light decorative backgrounds.
rows.avoid: Areas that must look solid.
rows.limits: Open fill: the fabric shows.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: A plain running-stitch line around the design.
rows.use: A light outline that tidies edges without weight.
rows.avoid: Badges and patches (use satin).
rows.limits: Width 0.8 to 6 mm.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: A satin band around the whole design; the classic badge edge.
rows.use: Badges, patches, round emblems.
rows.avoid: Logos on shirts, which usually have no border.
rows.limits: Width 1.6 to 6 mm. Placement inside, centre or outside the edge. Optional line inside (triple stitch 1.2 mm inside).
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Each stitch goes forward then back a little: a solid, hand-drawn line.
rows.use: Outlines that should look drawn by hand, redwork.
rows.avoid: Badge edges.
rows.limits: Width is the band it covers.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Slanted overlapping stitches: a rope-like line.
rows.use: Stems, vines, hand-embroidery outlines.
rows.avoid: Badge edges.
rows.limits: Width is the band it covers.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: A line with spikes into the shape, like a blanket edge.
rows.use: Appliqué edges, folk and kids' designs.
rows.avoid: Small designs where spikes crowd.
rows.limits: Width is the spike length.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: An open zigzag line around the design.
rows.use: Light decorative edges, casual looks.
rows.avoid: Clean badge edges (use satin).
rows.limits: Width is the band it covers.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: A line of repeated small shapes.
rows.use: Decorative frames.
rows.avoid: Small designs.
rows.limits: Shapes: diamond, triangle, scallop (motif setting).
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: A line held down by small crossing stitches, like cord laid on fabric.
rows.use: Cord-like frames, vintage looks.
rows.avoid: Small designs.
rows.limits: Width is the band it covers.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Out along the line and back through the same holes; every stitch sewn twice.
rows.use: Crisp heavy lines, blackwork and redwork.
rows.avoid: Badge edges.
rows.limits: 2 mm stitches.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Uneven stitches with gaps, like hand sewing.
rows.use: Rustic, hand-made frames.
rows.avoid: Clean professional edges.
rows.limits: Width is the band it covers.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: A running line with a raised knot at intervals.
rows.use: Vintage and cushion frames.
rows.avoid: Small designs.
rows.limits: Width is the knot size.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: A running line drawn as a repeating pattern.
rows.use: Decorative frames.
rows.avoid: Small designs.
rows.limits: Patterns: wave, loop, key (pattern setting).
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: 2.5 mm stitches, each starting halfway back along the last: a thick textured line.
rows.use: Bold frames that are lighter than satin.
rows.avoid: Fine designs.
rows.limits: Width is the band it covers.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: How many thread colours colour mode finds in the picture.
rows.use: Match the colours that matter in the art; each colour is a thread change.
rows.avoid: Too many: photo noise becomes scattered specks and many cuts.
rows.limits: 2 to 8.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Sews one found colour with another's thread, keeping the colour count.
rows.use: A colour scattered in many small pieces (many cuts in per_colour), near-duplicate shades.
rows.avoid: Colours that carry meaning in the art.
rows.limits: Up to 6 merges; replaces earlier merges.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Sets the area style and the row direction for every area of one thread colour.
rows.use: When the art asks for it: gradient for a sky, satin for lettering or stems, a different row direction for neighbouring colours so they catch the light differently.
rows.avoid: Changing colours the automatic choice already sews well; satin or puff on wide areas.
rows.limits: Up to 8 colours; replaces earlier choices. Parts a style does not suit keep the automatic choice: satin only where satin forms, puff only as wide as the foam, fills and textures only on parts wider than about 4.5 mm.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Colour areas smaller than this are merged into their neighbours.
rows.use: Specks, noise and tiny islands that cause cuts.
rows.avoid: Values so high that eyes, dots or small letters disappear.
rows.limits: 0 to 25 mm² (default 1).
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Smooths away fine detail before stitching.
rows.use: Busy pictures at small sizes, photo-like logos.
rows.avoid: Line art and text, which lose shape.
rows.limits: 0 to 100 (default 0).
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Smooths the boundaries between colour areas.
rows.use: Jagged edges from low-resolution pictures.
rows.avoid: Sharp corners and pixel art.
rows.limits: 0 to 3 (default 1).
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Sets the canvas height; the sewn design may be smaller because of margins.
rows.use: Match the person's size; rescale from the measured sewn size.
rows.avoid: Changing the person's size unless the design cannot sew at it; bigger means more stitches, cuts and time.
rows.limits: 3 to 400 mm. Lettering under about 5 mm capital height and parts under 1 mm do not sew cleanly.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Thin lines the fills lose are sewn on top as running stitches.
rows.use: Illustrations with fine linework: faces, highlights, hatching.
rows.avoid: Flat logos (adds clutter and stitches).
rows.limits: light: light lines only. all: dark lines too.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: true stitches the whole picture including the background; false keeps the saved subject cut-out.
rows.use: true only when the person wants the background sewn.
rows.avoid: Stitching a plain white or photo background the person did not ask for.
rows.limits: Colour mode only; line modes leave the background bare.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Removes boxes from the picture before stitching.
rows.use: Screenshot buttons, page dots, captions, watermarks, app frames.
rows.avoid: Boxes that cut into the art.
rows.limits: Up to 12 boxes in picture fractions; replaces earlier boxes.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Sets density, pull compensation, underlay, stitch length and tie-offs for the fabric, and the backing advice.
rows.use: Always match what it will be sewn on (t-shirt stretch_knit, polo pique, hoodie fleece, cap cap).
rows.avoid: Guessing when the person did not say: keep the current one.
rows.limits: The person's own saved fabrics are offered too.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: The sewing field the design must fit; designs bigger than it are split into several hoopings.
rows.use: Only when the person names their machine or hoop.
rows.avoid: Choosing one without being told.
rows.limits: Multi-hooping adds alignment work for the person.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Foam under 3D puff: 2 or 3 mm.
rows.use: 3 mm by default; 2 mm for smaller lettering (parts 2 to 6 mm wide).
rows.avoid: Setting it without puff.
rows.limits: 2 or 3 mm.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Row spacing, row angle, light thread and thread colour for photo_lines.
rows.use: Finer rows for detailed faces; light_thread for light thread on dark fabric.
rows.avoid: Rows under 0.8 mm on small designs (too dense).
rows.limits: row_mm 0.6 to 2, angle -180 to 180.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: How far the needle may travel back over sewn lines instead of cutting (line_art).
rows.use: Raise it when line art has many cuts.
rows.avoid: Very high values on fine art: retraced lines look heavier.
rows.limits: 2 to 30 mm (default 6).
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Light stitches sewn first under fills and satin to hold the fabric and lift the top stitches.
rows.use: Set by the fabric and the part width automatically: none under 1.5 mm, centre walk to 3 mm, edge run above, zigzag from 6 mm.
rows.avoid: Adding heavy underlay to tiny lettering.
rows.limits: Automatic; not a control.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Widens shapes slightly across the stitch direction because thread pulls fabric in.
rows.use: Set by the fabric; stretchy fabric needs more.
rows.avoid: Expecting thin parts to keep their exact width without it.
rows.limits: Automatic from the fabric.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Space between rows of fill or satin stitches (about 0.4 mm on most fabrics).
rows.use: Set by the fabric. Lighter for soft or stretchy fabric, fewer stitches, or when a sew-out was stiff; denser when a sew-out showed fabric through the fill.
rows.avoid: Very dense stitching on thin or stretchy fabric (puckers, holes).
rows.limits: lighter (rows 12% further apart), normal, denser (10% closer), for the whole design on top of the fabric. Foam keeps its own.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Same-colour parts that touch are joined without cutting; separate parts are sewn nearest first; each jump over bare fabric is cut.
rows.use: Read per_colour: many cuts in one colour mean scattered pieces; merge colours or small areas.
rows.avoid: Expecting joins across bare fabric: the file check fails any uncut jump.
rows.limits: Fewer pieces means fewer cuts.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Colours are sewn back to front: parts enclosed by others go first, fills grow slightly under later parts so no fabric shows between them.
rows.use: colours (default) for fewest colour changes; layers when parts lie inside other parts of a colour already used (an eye in a face) and must be sewn on top.
rows.avoid: Expecting a light colour sewn last to fully cover a dark one.
rows.limits: colours or layers. Layers can add colour changes.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Holes inside an area (the inside of an O, a ring) are left unsewn so the colour behind or the fabric shows.
rows.use: Keep holes that are part of the art. Sew over tiny holes that only add cuts, or holes holding a colour sewn later anyway.
rows.avoid: Satin on areas with holes (use tatami or offset fill).
rows.limits: Per thread colour: all holes, or only those up to a size in mm². Parts inside a hole that sew earlier are covered.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: The angle of fill rows or satin per area (0 = horizontal).
rows.use: Vary direction between neighbouring areas so they catch light differently; follow the shape for leaves and petals.
rows.avoid: Rows along a very long thin area (it pulls and narrows).
rows.limits: -180 to 180 degrees.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.

rows.does: Outlines between parts can be one thread colour or a darker shade of each part's thread.
rows.use: Cartoons and illustrations that have dark outlines in the art.
rows.avoid: Logos without outlines.
rows.limits: One running-stitch outline per edge between colours, sewn after all fills; one thread colour or a darker shade of each part (auto). Adds stitches and possibly a colour.
rows.source_note: Digitizer's handbook for Claude, 2026-10-28: written from Needler's own engine limits (NATIVE-ENGINE.md) and general digitizing practice.
